blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how to determine if a statement is true or false in mathematics? Let's explore logical reasoning!

blocks.markdown: Logical reasoning is a fundamental aspect of mathematics, helping us to evaluate statements and understand implications. In this lesson, we will learn how to identify true or false statements, write their negations, and interpret implications.

blocks.title: Statement
blocks.text: A statement is a declarative sentence that is either true or false, but not both.

blocks.markdown: Consider the statement: "Lagos is the capital of Nigeria." This statement is false because Abuja is the capital of Nigeria. Identifying the truth value of a statement is crucial in logical reasoning.

blocks.title: Negation of a Statement
blocks.prompt: Write the negation of the statement: "All students in the class passed the exam."

steps.text: Identify the original statement: "All students in the class passed the exam."
Negate the statement: "Not all students in the class passed the exam."

blocks.answer: The negation is: "Not all students in the class passed the exam."

blocks.markdown: In logical reasoning, an implication is a statement of the form "if $p$, then $q$". It suggests that whenever $p$ is true, $q$ must also be true.

blocks.title: Interpreting Implications
blocks.text: Remember that the implication "if $p$, then $q$" is only false when $p$ is true and $q$ is false.

points: A statement is either true or false.
The negation of a statement reverses its truth value.
An implication "if $p$, then $q$" is false only when $p$ is true and $q$ is false.
